title: cohort-entropy-adaptive-guard-and-rollforward
creator: Aisha Carter
description:
Problem:
Existing progressive delivery tooling at Redwood makes binary rollback decisions based mostly on single-threshold breaches (error rate or latency). This leads to noisy rollbacks for transient anomalies (CDN flaps, warmup tails) or unnecessary human intervention for recoverable blips. We need a more nuanced controller that can:
- allocate cohorts based on traffic entropy (behavioral diversity),
- evaluate multi-signal confidence windows, and
- support controlled 'rollforward' (promote despite small regressions) with tight safety envelopes and explicit roll-forward/rollback scoring.

Proposal (high level):
1) Cohort Entropy Allocator: create cohorts not only by percent traffic, region, and customer tier but also by entropy dimensions: prompt length distribution, session churn, device footprint, and feature-flag combinations. The allocator will sample deterministic cohorts so we can replay traffic slices in simulations.

2) Confidence Windows & Scoring: compute a rolling confidence window per cohort combining: success_rate_delta, p95/p99 latency delta, token-per-request distribution shift, error-mode kurtosis, and user-feedback signals (rate of degenerate responses). From these derive two scores: rollback_score and rollforward_score (both 0.0-1.0).

3) Rollforward Policy: if rollback_score < rollback_threshold but rollforward_score > rollforward_threshold for N consecutive windows, automatically promote cohort to next percentage bucket. Conversely, if rollback_score > threshold, trigger mitigation (attenuate, rollback, or variant swap).

4) Safety Nets and Limits: to avoid oscillation we will enforce:
   - max_promotions_per_release (default 3),
   - cool_down_period after a promotion (default 30m),
   - minimum sample size per window (statistical significance),
   - global rollback kill-switch accessible from Console and CLI.

5) Feature Flag Integration: rollout controller will require a rollout feature-flag key for every promotion. Flags support per-cohort overrides and emergency toggles. Naming scheme: rollout/<release>/<cohort-id> (see Console RFC link).

6) LTS Channel Rules: for LTS channels require a higher significance threshold and disallow automatic rollforward beyond 10% without manual approval from release owner. LTS promotions must include a signed release checklist (automated step in release pipeline).

7) Observability and Alerts: expose per-cohort metrics in Console, including rollforward_score/rollback_score, sample volume, and the hypothesis test p-values. Alerting rules: page on rollback_score > 0.9 OR p99 latency regression > 3x baseline AND sustained for 3 windows.

8) Simulation and QA: build a rollout-simulator that replays historical traffic traces with injected failure modes (network spikes, model cold starts, tokenization regressions) to validate thresholds. Target: 1000 simulated runs covering low/medium/high entropy cohorts.

Implementation plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (prototype, 2 sprints): allocator + scoring library + basic controller with CLI; unit tests and simulation harness.
- Phase 1 (dogfood, 2 cycles): integrate with internal dogfood cluster, exercise 5 internal releases, collect telemetry, tune thresholds.
- Phase 2 (beta): expose FF controls in Console, allow limited customer opt-in for non-LTS releases.
- Phase 3 (GA): enable for all non-LTS releases with default conservative thresholds; LTS still requires manual gating.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller correctly calculates scores and logs decisions in structured events (traceable to request IDs).
- Simulation shows >50% reduction in unnecessary rollbacks for transient anomaly classes while maintaining <=1% increase in time-to-fix for true regressions.
- Console shows per-cohort rollforward/rollback scores and allows emergency kill-switch.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect scoring permits a bad release to ramp. Mitigation: conservative defaults, multiple redundant signals, manual approval for LTS and >10% ramps.
- Risk: data lag causes stale decisions. Mitigation: require up-to-date sampling and enforce minimum freshness; fall back to conservative path when telemetry lag > 2 windows.
- Risk: complexity increases incident response time. Mitigation: clear runbooks, per-promotion audit trail, and an 'undo' command that reverts feature flags and traffic routing atomically.

Operational runbook excerpt (short):
- On high rollback_score page: hit Console rollback playbook -> Evaluate cohort traces -> If transient (single-window spike) attenuate to previous percent and re-evaluate in 15m.
- Emergency rollback: toggle rollout/<release>/* to off via CLI; controller will demote all cohorts within 30s.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RN/Entropy+Allocator+and+Rollforward+Design
- Rollout simulator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim/pull/112
- Console RFC for FF naming: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rXk-example-rfc
comments: 2026-02-15 - Priya Shah: Reviewed scoring approach. Suggested adding tokenization-shift as a separate signal; agreed and added to confidence window.
2026-02-20 - Luca Nguyen: Initial prototype landed (branch rollout/entropy-proto). Simulation harness integrated with historical trace subset. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987
2026-02-25 - Security (Marco Ruiz): Confirmed no extra secrets exposure for feature flags. Recommended audit logging for all FF toggles - added to acceptance criteria.

2026-02-27 - QA (Elena Park): Ran 200 simulated runs; observed decreased rollback churn for warmup spikes. Found edge case where small cohorts (<0.1% traffic) report noisy stats; added minimum_sample_size enforcement.
2026-03-01 - Product (Nadia Gomez): OK to proceed to dogfood after tuning thresholds. Reminder: LTS channel requires manual sign-off before any >10% promotion.
